title: Cap. VII open: De Reprobatione — prolegomena; two rocks to avoid
pass_a_gloss: Certain prolegomena concerning Reprobation together with the Arminian opinion. These things having been tasted beforehand, I shall presently approach the other part of the undertaken disputation, which is concerning passing by, non-election or Reprobation of those persons whom God has not dignified with that excellent and special mercy which infallibly leads to life. And here, and everywhere, that Pauline saying ought to obtain, Rom. 12:3: not to think more highly than one ought to think. For there will only be wanting for idle curiosity to learn as much as it shall please to inquire, as Tertullian wisely, On the Soul, at the end. In this matter therefore to be treated, there are two rocks to be fled with all caution.
pass_b_english: Cap. VII — some prolegomena on Reprobation, with the Arminian view. Preliminaries tasted, I turn next to the other half of the dispute: passing by, non-election, or Reprobation of those God has not dignified with that excellent special mercy that infallibly leads to life. Here and everywhere Paul's word must hold (Rom. 12:3): not to think beyond what one ought. Idle curiosity will always find as much to learn as it cares to ask (so Tertullian wisely, On the Soul, at the end). In treating this matter, two rocks must be fled with all caution.
source_text: De Reprobatione quaedam prolegomena una cum sententia Arminiana. Hisce praelibatis, alteram susceptae disputationis partem mox aggrediar, quae est de praeteritione, non-electione sive Reprobatione illarum personarum quas Deus eximia illa et speciali misericordia, quae ad vitam infallibiliter perducit, non est dignatus. Atque hic, et uspiam, obtinere debet illud Paulinum, Rom. xii. 3. μὴ ὑπερφρονεῖν παρ' ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν. Nam otiosae curiositati tantum deerits discere, quantum libuerit inquirere, ut prudenter Tertullianus, De anima, in fine. In hac ergo materia tractanda duo scopuli sunt omni cautione fugiendi.
